name: PagerDuty
scope_notes: SaaS; REST API on current plans, user token keys need Advanced Permissions, Audit Trail on Business/Enterprise for Incident Management/Digital Operations (legacy); SCIM uses general access keys or app OAuth tokens.

controls.name: Disable general access REST API key
controls.what: Stops the key working with the REST API without deleting it; can be re-enabled.
controls.setting: Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys > Disable

controls.name: Delete (Remove) general access REST API key
controls.setting: Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys > Remove

controls.name: Read-only API Key
controls.what: Restricts a general access key to GET calls.
controls.setting: Create New API Key > Read-only API Key checkbox

controls.name: Delete another user's API user token
controls.what: Admins/Account Owner can delete other users' personal keys, except keys of Account Owner, Admins or Global Admins.

controls.name: User permissions bound user tokens
controls.what: User token requests are limited to the user's own permissions.

controls.name: Install (admin approval) of public OAuth apps
controls.what: A public Scoped OAuth app cannot access the account until an Admin installs it and approves its scopes.
controls.setting: App installation page > Install on your account

controls.name: Revoke All User Tokens
controls.what: Admin revokes every user token issued for an installed app; runs in the background.
controls.setting: Integrations > OAuth Apps > (app) > Revoke All User Tokens

controls.name: Uninstall
controls.what: Revokes all user tokens for the app and blocks reauthorization until reinstalled.

controls.name: Revoke All Tokens (App Registration)
controls.what: App owner invalidates all OAuth tokens issued to the app.
controls.setting: Integrations > Developer Tools > App Registration > app > OAuth Client > Revoke All Tokens

controls.name: Scoped OAuth scopes
controls.what: Per-resource read/write scopes (e.g. incidents.read) limit what the token can call.

controls.name: Delete all OAuth delegations
controls.what: Revokes a user's mobile or web delegations (signs them out).

controls.name: Change Another User's Password
controls.what: Admin password change also revokes the user's OAuth tokens.
controls.setting: People > Users > user > User Settings > Change Password

controls.name: Generate a new integration key
controls.setting: Services > Service Directory > service > Integrations > Edit Integration > Generate a new integration key

controls.name: Delete Integration
controls.what: Deletes the integration and its key; cannot be recovered.

controls.name: Base role: personal REST API key permission
controls.what: Under Advanced Permissions, every base role except Limited Stakeholder can create personal REST API keys; assigning Limited Stakeholder removes the ability.
controls.plan: Plans with Advanced Permissions (Professional, Business, Enterprise for Incident Management, Digital Operations legacy, PD Reliability Platform)

controls.name: App Registration role requirement
controls.what: Only Manager, Global Admin, or Account Owner base roles can register apps, so lower roles cannot create private OAuth apps.

controls.name: Manager role required for integration keys
controls.what: Only users with a Manager role or above can generate Events API integration keys.

no_control.what: No IP/network restriction for REST API keys; the IP allow list explicitly excludes REST API calls.
No IP/network restriction for user token keys.
No IP/network restriction for OAuth app tokens.
No IP/network restriction for OAuth user tokens.
No IP restriction on Events API traffic.
Deleting an app's OAuth functionality does not revoke tokens already issued.
Admins cannot delete user token keys belonging to the Account Owner, Admins or Global Admins.

controls_unknown: Whether general access or user token keys can be given an expiry, or ever expire.
Whether SSO enforcement or deprovisioning in the IdP affects existing API keys (only "user leaves the account" disables user keys).
Any admin setting to block users from creating user token keys or to block Classic User OAuth app authorization.
Whether API key create/disable/delete events appear in the Audit Trail (the tracked resource list does not include API keys).
Whether disabling/deleting a key or Revoke All User Tokens ends in-flight access immediately (Revoke All runs in the background).
Whether private app (client credentials) tokens can be revoked by admins other than the app owner; client secret expiry/rotation.
Whether read (GET) API calls are logged anywhere customer-visible.
Whether integration key creation/rotation appears in audit records (support page says integration add/remove is not captured; Audit API lists Integrations as an associated resource of Services).

credentials.name: General Access REST API Key (account API key)

authentication.summary: 20-character account-level key created by an Admin or Account Owner, sent as 'Authorization: Token token=<key>'. Not tied to the creating user; full or read-only access to all account data.

federation.details: Static shared secret; no workload/OIDC federation documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP Allow List for User Sessions covers web/mobile logins only; REST API calls are explicitly excluded.

renewal.expiry_basis: No documented expiry; key works until disabled or deleted.
renewal.summary: Rotate manually: create new key, update clients, delete old.

administration.summary: Admins/Account Owner create, disable, re-enable and delete under Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys. Table shows description, creation date, access level, disabled status; no last-used date documented.
administration.conditions: REST API available on current pricing plans; also used for SCIM provisioning.

offboard.details: Account API keys are tied to the account, not to the user who created them.

inventory.details: Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys table lists every general access key with status.

log_sources.name: Audit Trail (UI + GET /audit/records)
log_sources.notes: Business, Enterprise for Incident Management, Digital Operations (legacy); 12-month retention; config changes on users, teams, schedules, escalation policies, services, IP allow lists only. Admin / global API token, scope audit_records.read.

credential_id_fields.notes: Last 4 chars of the token when method.type=api_token.

lifecycle_events.notes: Config changes made with the key; reads not documented as logged.

anomaly_cues: Config changes with method.type=api_token from unexpected remote_address
Changes to IP allow lists, users or roles via api_token
Bulk incident or user reads (not visible in audit)

containment.steps: Integrations > Developer Tools > API Access Keys: Disable (reversible) or Remove (permanent). Issue a replacement key first if SCIM or recovery depends on it.
containment.notes: Docs say a disabled key stops working with the REST API; timing not stated. Keep one key for IP-allow-list lockout recovery.

calls.log_notes: Audit records cover config changes only.

calls.reveals: Incident log entries across the account
Enriched incident data; account keys need no team/service filter
All users on the account (names, emails, roles)
calls.log_notes: Audit records cover configuration changes only; reads are not listed as audited.

unknown: GET /users/me does not work with account keys, so no whoami for this credential.

credentials.name: User Token REST API Key (personal REST API key)

authentication.summary: 20-character key created by a user in My Profile > User Settings > API Access; requests run with that user's permissions. Same Token header format as account keys.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP allow list does not restrict REST API calls.

lifetime.summary: No expiry documented; disabled if user leaves

renewal.summary: Lost or rotated keys are deleted and recreated.

administration.summary: Requires Advanced Permissions. Any base role from Restricted Access up can create their own keys. Admins can delete other users' keys except those of Account Owner, Admins or Global Admins. Table shows last used date.
administration.conditions: Advanced Permissions accounts only. No admin setting to disable user key creation is documented.

offboard.details: Docs say a user API key is disabled when the user leaves the account.

offboard.ui: People > Users > user name > Delete User (Advanced Permissions accounts go through the Offboarding flow)

log_sources.name: Audit Trail (UI + GET /audit/records)
log_sources.notes: Business, Enterprise for Incident Management, Digital Operations (legacy); 12-month retention; config changes on users, teams, schedules, escalation policies, services, IP allow lists only. Admin / global API token, scope audit_records.read.

credential_id_fields.notes: Presumed acting user; not explicitly documented for user keys.

anomaly_cues: Check last used date in User Settings API Access table
Admin-user tokens used for config changes

containment.steps: User or Admin: User Settings > API Access > Remove. Removing the user from the account disables their keys.
containment.notes: Admins cannot remove keys of Admins/Global Admins/Account Owner; those users must remove their own.

calls.reveals: Users the key owner can see
calls.log_notes: Audit records cover configuration changes only.

credentials.name: Scoped OAuth app token (private app, client credentials)

authentication.summary: A private app with Scoped OAuth exchanges client_id/client_secret at https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/token (client_credentials) for a Bearer token limited only by the app's scopes, not by any user.

federation.details: No workload identity federation documented; client secret only.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP allow list does not restrict REST API calls.

lifetime.summary: Access token 1 day; client secret no documented expiry

renewal.summary: App requests a new token with its client secret; no refresh token.

administration.summary: Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner can register apps under Integrations > Developer Tools > App Registration. Private apps need no install review and are not in the OAuth Apps list (Manage Private Apps instead).
administration.conditions: App tokens are only issued on the account that created the app.

offboard.details: Client-credentials app tokens have no user involved.

inventory.details: Private apps are listed under OAuth Apps > Manage Private Apps (and App Registration > My Apps); issued app tokens are not listed.

expiry.api: Fixed 1-day lifetime; POST https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/token response field expires_in

token_format.notes: Documented example access token is "pdus+_EXAMPLE_KEY_ID_EXAMPLE_TOKEN"; prefix not formally specified.

log_sources.name: Audit Trail (UI + GET /audit/records)
log_sources.notes: Business, Enterprise for Incident Management, Digital Operations (legacy); 12-month retention; config changes on users, teams, schedules, escalation policies, services, IP allow lists only. Admin / global API token, scope audit_records.read.

anomaly_cues: app_reference actors you do not recognize
Private apps created by Managers without review

containment.steps: App Registration > app > OAuth Client > Revoke All Tokens, then delete and recreate OAuth functionality to replace the client secret (revoke first: deleting does not revoke tokens).
containment.notes: Docs say Revoke All Tokens invalidates all tokens; app tokens otherwise expire in 1 day.

calls.log_notes: Audit records cover configuration changes only.

unknown: Whether GET /users/me works with an app token.

credentials.name: User OAuth token (Scoped OAuth and Classic User OAuth apps)

authentication.summary: Authorization-code + PKCE flow; the user logs in and consents, and the app gets a Bearer token acting as that user, limited to the intersection of app scopes and user permissions. Classic apps use coarse read/write scopes.

federation.details: The grant requires an interactive user login, which goes through the account login (SSO if configured); whether SSO policy is rechecked on refresh is not documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP allow list applies to web/mobile sessions, not REST API calls or integrations.

lifetime.summary: Scoped: 1-day access, 30-day refresh, 1-year window. Classic: 30-day access, 210-day refresh, 3-year window.

renewal.expiry_basis: Refresh token inactivity (30 d scoped / 210 d classic) within a rolling window (1 y / 3 y).
renewal.summary: Refresh grant returns new access and refresh tokens.

administration.summary: Public Scoped OAuth apps must be installed by an Admin, who approves scopes; Admins see who authorized, revoke all tokens, or uninstall. Classic apps work across accounts once created and appear in the installed list once authorized.
administration.conditions: Admin install gate applies to public Scoped OAuth apps; Classic app gating not stated.

inventory.details: Integrations > OAuth Apps: for each installed app admins see everyone who authorized it and when. Private apps are managed on a separate page.

expiry.api: Fixed lifetimes (Scoped 1 day/30 days/1 year; Classic 30 days/210 days/3 years); token response from https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/token field expires_in

token_format.notes: Example tokens "pdus+_EXAMPLE_KEY_ID_EXAMPLE_TOKEN"; an id_token JWT is also returned.

log_sources.name: Audit Trail (UI + GET /audit/records)
log_sources.notes: Business, Enterprise for Incident Management, Digital Operations (legacy); 12-month retention; config changes on users, teams, schedules, escalation policies, services, IP allow lists only. Admin / global API token, scope audit_records.read.

lifecycle_events.notes: Installing an app creates an audit trail event; exact name not documented.

anomaly_cues: New installs or unknown authorizers on OAuth Apps page

containment.steps: Integrations > OAuth Apps > app > Revoke All User Tokens or Uninstall; per-user: DELETE /oauth_delegations or admin password change.
containment.notes: Revoke All runs in the background; delegation deletion is synchronous.

unknown: Exact audit event names for install/uninstall/revoke

calls.reveals: Incidents visible to user within scopes
Users the authorizing person can see (needs users.read scope)
calls.log_notes: Audit records cover configuration changes only.

authentication.summary: 32-character key on a service (or Event Orchestration) integration, sent in the event body as routing_key to https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue. Can only send events (create/ack/resolve alerts, change events), not read data.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP allow list does not affect Events API traffic.

renewal.summary: 'Generate a new integration key' overwrites the key immediately.

administration.summary: Manager role or above can create integrations and keys; rotate or delete on the service Integrations tab.
administration.conditions: Events API available on all accounts.

offboard.details: Integration keys belong to a service integration, not a user.

inventory.details: Keys are shown per service on the service's Integrations tab; no account-wide key list found.

inventory.ui: Services > Service Directory > service > Integrations tab > expand integration > Integration Key (per service)

token_format.notes: 32-character string; ruleset keys begin with R.

log_sources.name: Incident/alert log entries (GET /log_entries)
log_sources.notes: Events produce alerts/incidents; no per-key audit documented. Audit Trail does not capture integration add/remove.

anomaly_cues: Unexpected incidents/alerts or change events on a service

containment.steps: Services > service > Integrations > Edit Integration > Generate a new integration key, or Delete Integration.
containment.notes: Rotation overwrites the key immediately; old key presumably rejected (not stated).

unknown: Any log of Events API sends by key beyond the resulting alerts/incidents
